title: Week 7: DDPG, RLHF and multi-agent RL

sections.heading: RLHF: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback ( rl/rlhf.py )
Multi-agent RL and game theory 101 ( rl/marl.py )

text: DDPG: continuous actions ( rl/ddpg.py ). DQN needs max a Q(s,a) , which is intractable for continuous a . DDPG learns a deterministic actor mu phi(s) that approximates the argmax, trained by the deterministic policy gradient: nabla phi J approx E sbig[nabla a Q(s, a; theta)big a = mu phi(s) , nabla phi mu phi(s)big]. In code this is just actor loss = −Q(s, mu (s)).mean() . - Critic target: y = r + gamma (1 - d) ,Q'(s', mu'(s')) , using target networks updated by Polyak averaging, theta' leftarrow tautheta + (1-tau)theta' with tau = 0.005. - Exploration: Gaussian noise on the action, since a deterministic policy never explores on its own. - Pendulum-v1 (30k steps, 3 seeds): greedy return −146.7 ± 2.3 . The pendulum swings up and balances; a random policy scores roughly −1200. RLHF: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback ( rl/rlhf.py ). Used to align large language models. There are three stages: supervised fine-tuning → reward model from human preferences → RL against that reward with a KL penalty . The toy version here keeps the two RL-specific ideas, with "responses" represented as 20 arms with hidden true quality. 1. Bradley–Terry reward model. Humans compare two responses. We model P(i succ j) = sigma(r i - r j) and fit hat r by maximising the log-likelihood sum log sigma(hat r w - hat r l) , which is logistic regression on reward differences. Rewards are identifiable only up to a constant. comparisons 50 100 250 500 1,000 2,500 5,000 % of response pairs ranked correctly 72.0 77.5 85.7 90.2 93.2 95.6 96.7 2. KL-regularised policy. Maximising E pi[hat r] - beta ,KL(pi , , pi ref) has the closed-form solution pi (a) propto pi ref(a) ,exp(hat r(a) / beta) . (Derivation: the objective equals -beta ,KL(pi , , pi ) + const.) The KL term keeps the policy close to the reference model. That limits reward hacking , i.e. over-exploiting errors in hat r . At beta = 1 the true expected reward rises from −0.18 (reference) to 0.41 , for KL = 0.28 nats. Smaller beta moves along the curve towards the best response. Multi-agent RL and game theory 101 ( rl/marl.py ). With several learners, each agent's environment is non-stationary , because the other agents are learning too. The solution concept becomes the Nash equilibrium : no player can gain by changing strategy unilaterally. Game Pure Nash Mixed Nash (indifference conditions) Learning result Prisoner's dilemma (Defect, Defect) none Independent Q-learners defect 95% of the time ( epsilon = 0.1 exploration accounts for the rest), even though (C, C) pays both players more Matching pennies none each plays heads with p = 0.5 Fictitious play converges to empirical frequencies of 0.498 / 0.498 The mixed equilibrium comes from making the opponent indifferent: if player 2 plays heads with prob. q , then player 1 is indifferent when q A 00 + (1-q) A 01 = q A 10 + (1-q) A 11 , which gives q = 1/2 . Reading: Lillicrap et al., DDPG (2016); Christiano et al., "Deep RL from Human Preferences" (2017); Ouyang et al., InstructGPT (2022); Albrecht, Christianos & Schäfer, "Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning" (MARL Book), Ch. 1–4; Shimon Whiteson's MARL seminar.
